PALETTE EXPLORER
About the colours

From architecture to palette.

Papers come from the Paper Notes CVPR 2026 and NeurIPS 2026 indexes. Figures come from original papers or public author projects; each card identifies its source and figure number.

We sample module fills, outlines and tokens, then visually check the original pixels. Backgrounds, example photos and noise are excluded; meaningful neutral colours are retained. Each palette has 2–8 exact representative colours. Swatches have equal widths, not proportional areas. Gradients use a representative sample.

Tags describe the paper’s task and model. Colour notes are editorial analysis; English descriptions are machine-assisted translations. Original figure labels stay as published. Figure rights belong to their authors; follow the source licence when reusing them.

Likes start at zero, can be undone and are saved in this browser. The ranking reflects your local likes, not a shared site-wide count. Ties follow collection order.
